why: `classdef Mid < Base & Base` lists `Base` twice. MATLAB rejects a class listed twice among its superclasses, so MATLAB states nothing here, and the truth holds only what project rules say: each written superclass reference is kept at its own place (its name's column, step 14); a reference no resolution pass answers is kept as a failed row, which a later sync retries (#1240; the row lifecycle in src/db/schema.sql); and a sync ends where a fresh index ends, counts included. When the class folder `@Base` turns binary, `Base` is no class, and a fresh index keeps a failed `extends:Base` row for each reference: so must a sync (found by the step 11 fuzzer).

known.what: Until step 14 a sync kept one failed row where a fresh index kept two.
known.why: Both references were written at the start of the superclass list (column 13, not at their names), so while `Base` resolved they made one edge (the store keeps one edge per source, target, kind, line and column), which a sync turned back into one row. Step 4 had accepted this as two references on one line merging; the cause was the shared place, and each reference now has its own.
